youtube.title: 115 People Vanished. They Left Behind One Word. | The Lost Colony of Roanoke
youtube.description:
In 1587, about 115 English settlers landed on Roanoke Island, off present-day North Carolina. Their governor, John White, sailed to England for supplies, leaving behind his granddaughter Virginia Dare, the first English child born in the Americas. War with Spain and the Spanish Armada kept him away for three years. When he returned in August 1590, the settlement was abandoned. The colonists had agreed to carve a cross if they were forced to leave; there was none. The only clue was the word CROATOAN carved on a post: the name of a nearby island and its people. Bad weather forced White to leave before he could search it, and he never found the colonists.

📂 Case File #027: The Lost Colony of Roanoke

Sources: North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources, "The Origins of the Lost Colony Mystery"; History.com, "What Happened to the 'Lost Colony' of Roanoke?".
Images (Wikimedia Commons): Lost Colony tree replica and Fort Raleigh earthworks by Sarah Stierch (CC BY 4.0); Baptism of Virginia Dare (engraving), John White map study (British Museum), Roanoke Island map (1917), Hendrik Frans Schaefels, The Defeat of the Spanish Armada; Bonaventura Peeters, Sea storm with sailing ships (public domain).
Narration voice: AI.
